Column 8 (Y house price of unit area) 
4. What

input 
columns 
mean 
? 
 
X1 - Transaction date 
X2 - House age (unit: year) 
X3 - Distance to the nearest MRT station (unit: meter) 
X4 - Number of convenience stores in the living circle on foot  
X5 - The geographic coordinate, latitude. (unit: degree) 
X6 -The geographic coordinate, longitude. (unit: degree)

Page 2/6 
Section B 
 
1. Understanding the dataset [4 marks] 
There are many input variables in this dataset. Use only X1 to X4 as input 
variables, and y as the output variable. 
Using the scatter plots between each of the input features (X1-X4) and the 
output (Y), which input variable, do you think, is better in predicting 
the output / target variable ? 
 
 
 
Ans: The input variable “X3 - Distance to the nearest MRT Station” is 
better in predicting the target variable. As X3 - Distance to the nearest MRT

Page 3/6 
Station increases , the Y-house price tends to decrease (negatively 
correlated scatter plot) 
 
2. Write code to find out how many samples are there in total in this 
dataset? [1 mark] 
 
 
3. What is the train test split ratio that you have chosen ? [1 Mark] 
 
● Here the train-test ratio is 80:20. 
● 80% of the data is used for training and remaining 20% is used for 
testing

Page 4/6 
4. Evaluate the linear regression model by computing the MAE, MSE and 
Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).  
 
 
[3 marks] 
 
● Model using X1-X6 input variables

Page 6/6 
 
5. What are the 3 new things that you learned after you completed this 
assignment ? 
● Learned how to evaluate the performance of the model by using 
different  metrics like MAE, MSE and MAPE. 
● Learned the significance of MAPE which gives the absolute 
percentage difference between the model’s predicted and actual 
value (relative error). MAPE supports multi-output (where the model 
predicts multiple output variables). 
● Learned how the train-test split ratio affects the model performance.
